author: ansel
text: sc-323: N = 3 consecutive timeouts (probe timeout or pool wait) open the breaker; a success resets the count; a connection-class error opens it at once; a half-open trial that times out reopens it (it was just failing).

author: ansel
text: sc-324: a row is used only when its query_key equals the key of our own fixed summary query (REPORT_SUMMARY / report_summaries_query(n)) for its stored params, and those params give exact codes equal to its report_codes: the model's run_wcl_graphql can name a query ReportSummary but can't forge that key. Bounded by migration 0020: partial index on raw_fetches(fetched_at DESC) WHERE operation_name IN the two summary ops; SET LOCAL statement_timeout 2 s; the DB projects code/title/startTime/zone.name/actor names instead of returning full payloads. No players lookup column (YAGNI).

author: ansel
text: sc-326: a turn that waited on another process's Redis lock and got its value counts external even if that process answered from the DB store: it can't be told apart and over-counting external is the safe side. Same-process cache single-flight passes 'went to WCL' from the shared load to every joiner.

author: ansel
text: sc-255: add_message locks the conversation row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, tenant-scoped) before max(seq)+1; concurrent adds to one conversation serialise. No retry loop, no new column. SQLite ignores FOR UPDATE (single connection anyway).

author: nils
text: sc-334 Compact big report tables: tables get their own cap of 40,000 chars (= the 10k-token budget at chars/4), not the 60k MAX_JSON_CHARS; at or under it a table is unchanged. Over it: top 25 rows per list (sorted by total, auras by totalUptime), scalar fields only, class/spec split from icon, per_second from totalTime, <list>_omitted counts; shrinks to 10, then 5 rows if still over; else note only. Never a _preview. Other _acap users untouched.

author: nils
text: sc-334: a compact table sets completeness.truncated only when rows were omitted (some list has omitted > 0). Dropped per-row breakdowns (abilities, targets, gear, talents) are named in the note with how to narrow (source_id). Reason: VALIDATION_BEFORE_ANALYSIS tells the model to fetch the rest whenever truncated is true, which is exactly the per-player fan-out we are removing.

author: nils
text: sc-302 Big-report turn ends with no answer: the no-answer message applies to chat turns only, i.e. stream_response called with a workspace user_id (ws.py passes str(tenant_id)); greeting and guide jobs run as the legacy local user and keep today's empty result (otherwise the greeting cache or a guild summary could store the message). Covers 'no text after the last tool result' and also 'no text at all'. Outcome set via TurnStats.outcome='empty'. No ws.py change.

author: nils
text: sc-328 Mark search results as data: each hit text becomes '<data>...</data>'; every '<' and '>' inside the hit text is replaced by '‹' / '›', so no tag (closing or opening, any spelling) can appear inside a block. Chunk text caps: report title 80 chars, guild name 40 chars (chunks.bounded).

author: nils
text: sc-339 Recent-raid kickoff pre-fetch: runs via services.background.spawn (fresh context, GC-safe) keyed ('kickoff_prefetch', tenant_id, report_code): one in flight per workspace+report (a per-report-only key would let workspace A's run swallow B's click while B's turn then pays full WCL cost). Acts as the clicking user's identity (current_identity) so the fetch sink grants to that workspace exactly as its own chat turn would; refresh actor stays None (no turn, never forces a refresh). Calls the agent's own tool functions (load_report_summary, get_report_table(code,'Summary',fight_id=F)) so query keys match byte for byte. Bound: 1 summary + at most 10 tables = 11 WCL requests. Boss pick: per (encounter, difficulty) the last kill, else the last pull. Only when the fetch writer runs (app.state.fetch_writer) - without the store it would warm nothing.
